title: F2 blocked until Plan G closes; reduced-evidence override is the only bypass
body:
Sequencing locked at Plan G lock turn (2026-05-06): F2 (Goal Governance V1 post-impl completion-test + journey-walk auditor) stays at status: draft until Plan G closes. The only legitimate bypass is an explicit reduced-evidence D-entry recorded in F2's plan dir naming exactly which evidence sources are deferred and why.

Why: F2's whole value depends on runtime evidence. Without the harness, the post-impl audit collapses into text review and blurs back into F1's pre-impl sufficiency layer. Sequencing G first prevents F2 from shipping as a paper-only audit.

How to apply: when F2 lock proposal arrives, validate that Plan G is at status: completed OR a reduced-evidence D-entry exists in F2's plan dir. Refuse the F2 lock otherwise.

title: Plan G is capture-only, not audit
body:
Plan G ships per-source evidence collectors that write structured `EvidenceRef` artifacts. Plan G does NOT ship audit, scoring, journey-walk semantics, or assertions about whether captured evidence proves a journey passed.

Why: separating capture from audit keeps two failure modes apart — 'we couldn't get the screenshot' is a different bug class from 'the screenshot proves the journey is broken'. Forcing them into one feature would make both harder to debug and would leak audit semantics into infrastructure that other plans should be able to consume.

How to apply: any temptation to add 'does this evidence pass the contract?' logic during G1-G5 implementation belongs in F2. Plan G adapters return EvidenceRef lists; that's the contract.

title: Evidence path convention: evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/<source>/<journey-id>/<artifact>
body:
Plan G writes captured artifacts under `evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/<source>/<journey-id>/<artifact>` mirroring F0's `pre_impl/` convention. Reuses `nested_orchestration.goal_governance_evidence_path()` so the path discipline stays in one place.

Source values: `web`, `ios`, `android`, `backend/<provider>` (where provider ∈ {firebase, supabase, generic}).

Why: a uniform path convention is what lets F2 walk evidence without source-specific logic in the auditor.

How to apply: every G adapter MUST write through `goal_governance_evidence_path(plan_dir, 'post_impl', f'{source}/{journey_id}/{artifact}')`. Greppable invariant — no ad-hoc path construction allowed.

title: Project-agnostic invariant inherited from F1 D013
body:
Plan G adapters are GENERIC. No project-name special cases under `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/runtime_evidence/`. No `spin_dine_*`, `glam_*`, `creator_hub_*`, `styln_*`, `android_parity_*` modules, classes, or branches.

Project-specific configuration (which Firebase project, which simulator device, which Playwright base URL, which adb device serial, which Android package name) lives in operator-edited config files, NOT in adapter code.

Why: F2 must consume Plan G's harness for any plan regardless of which projects its journeys touch. Coupling adapters to specific projects would (a) defeat F2's project-agnostic positioning, (b) make every new project an adapter change, (c) blur the line between infrastructure and product.

How to apply: F005 (G5) acceptance includes a greppable assertion that the harness core is source-agnostic. Each adapter (F001-F004) acceptance includes greppable assertions that operator config (URLs, device ids, project ids, package names) is not hardcoded.

title: No new credential storage in Plan G
body:
Backend adapters use existing auth surfaces where available; Firebase ships first because it has the F022 service account precedent. Supabase + Generic provider support MUST NOT introduce new credential storage in Plan G — the operator passes credentials at runtime (env var or session config), Plan G transports them but never persists.

Why: credential storage is its own decision class with its own threat model (where do keys live? how are they rotated? who can read them?). Plan G is infrastructure plumbing, not auth infrastructure. Folding credential storage in here would stretch G's scope and create operational debt.

How to apply: F004 (G4) acceptance includes the sanitization invariant that no credential bytes leak into logs or output paths. `runtime_evidence/backend/` modules MUST NOT write credential values to disk. If a future adapter needs persistent auth (e.g., OAuth refresh tokens for a SaaS provider), that's a follow-up plan with its own credential-storage design.

title: Cross-vendor dogfood dispatcher queued as separate follow-up plan
body:
F005 close-out from Plan F1 noted that the cross-vendor production dispatcher (real Codex auditor for F003's `dispatch=` seam) remains queued. Plan G does NOT bundle that work. Plan G is capture-only; the cross-vendor invariant is an audit-time concern that engages when F2 ships.

Why: G's failure modes (no simulator, no device, no network) are independent of which vendor runs the auditor. Folding the cross-vendor wiring into G would conflate two unrelated concerns and inflate G's scope.

How to apply: when drafting the cross-vendor dogfood dispatcher follow-up plan, note that Plan G has zero auditor-vendor coupling and the dispatcher plan can ship independently. Plan G's adapters are vendor-neutral by construction.

title: agent-conventions schema verified — no v1.5.0 bump needed; Plan G is single-repo
body:
Verified at Plan G lock turn: every G adapter's output type maps to an existing v1.4.0 `EvidenceRef.type` enum value:

- G1 (web): screenshot, log (console), file (DOM/trace/video), url (hosted resources)
- G2 (iOS): screenshot, log (simctl), file (crash report)
- G3 (Android): screenshot, log (logcat), file (tombstone/ANR), test_output (Espresso/Gradle reports)
- G4 (backend): log (cloud logging), url (signed URLs), file (JSONL exports)

All map cleanly. No agent-conventions schema changes needed. Plan G is single-repo (DontPanic only); no two-commit cross-repo boundary like F1's F001+F002.

How to apply: if during implementation a G adapter surfaces an artifact type not in the existing enum, STOP and surface a schema-bump amendment as its own decision entry — do not coerce the artifact into a wrong type. The v1.4.0 enum should be sufficient; a real schema gap is a planning failure worth flagging.

title: Reduced-evidence override recorded in F2's plan dir, not Plan G's
body:
F2 may declare a reduced-evidence D-entry deferring one or more of G1-G4 (e.g. 'this F2-derived child plan ships without iOS evidence because the journey doesn't touch iOS'). The defer entry lives in F2's plan dir, NOT in Plan G's.

Why: keeping defer decisions in the consumer plan (F2 / each F2-derived child) preserves Plan G as a stable infrastructure plan. Plan G is a binary 'closed/not-closed' surface; consumers decide which sources their journey needs.

How to apply: F2's lock template should include a 'evidence_sources_used' field listing which G adapters the plan exercises. Any source NOT in that list requires an explicit defer-D-entry with an operator-supplied reason. F2's gate validates the list against Plan G's status.

title: Android v1 is capture-only — DontPanic does not own Android test orchestration
body:
G3 (Android) ships two capture-only modes:

- `passive_observe` — adb screencap/logcat/tombstone/ANR collection against an existing operator-driven device/session.
- `post_hoc_ingest` — consume artifacts from existing Gradle/Espresso/Maestro/CI output.

G3 does NOT run tests. No `gradlew test`, no `am instrument`, no `./gradlew connectedAndroidTest`, no `mvn test` invocation anywhere in `runtime_evidence/android.py`. F003 acceptance includes a greppable assertion enforcing this.

Why: Android test orchestration is a much larger surface (multiple build systems, multiple test runners, device matrix management, flake handling). Plan G's job is to make F2 useful for Android plans; making DontPanic own Android test execution is a separate plan with its own scope.

How to apply: full Android MCP/test orchestration is a follow-up plan, triggered by real-world signal that operators want DontPanic-driven Android dispatch (per the demand-driven v2 planning memory). Until that signal arrives, G3 stays capture-only and operators bring their own test runner.

title: Backend observability is provider-adapter based; no Firebase-specific assumptions in the harness
body:
G4 (backend) is built around a `BackendCollectorRegistry` resolving provider name → adapter. v1 ships three adapters:

- Firebase — production-ready, reuses F022 SA.
- Supabase — provider slot only; interface implemented + fixture tests; production paths raise NotImplementedError until a follow-up plan wires it.
- Generic — operator-supplied HTTP endpoint / log file / JSONL export with operator-supplied runtime credentials.

**No Firebase-specific assumptions in the registry, in G4's interface, or in G5's harness core.** F004 acceptance includes greppable assertions that Firebase fast-paths exist only inside `firebase.py`.

Why: Firebase happened to be the existing auth precedent (F022) but DontPanic must not couple itself to one backend vendor. Coupling would make Supabase/HTTP/log-file projects second-class citizens and reproduce the cross-vendor invariant violation from D006 in a different layer.

How to apply: future backend adapters (BigQuery, Datadog, Honeycomb, etc.) ship as their own plans adding `BackendEvidenceCollector` implementations + registering with the registry. The harness core never grows backend-vendor branches.

title: Plan G uses F001-F005 feature IDs while prose may refer to G1-G5
body:
features.json uses the F001-F005 feature ID convention required by agent-conventions schema (`^F\d{3}$`). Prose in plan.md, decisions.jsonl, and close-out memos may refer to G1-G5 for roadmap clarity. Both naming surfaces are correct; the table in plan.md maps between them.

Why: schema conformance is non-negotiable (the validator + every existing tool keys off F\d{3}). Roadmap names like 'G1' carry useful sequencing intent ('the first prerequisite') that F001 doesn't. Mapping table preserves both.

How to apply: when implementing G1, the commit message + features.json + tests reference F001; the close-out memo prose may say 'G1 (F001)' for clarity. Any future Plan G* references should preserve the same mapping.

title: G1 (F001) close-out — Web evidence collector shipped with pluggable driver and v1 default-driver skip
body:
G1 sealed in DontPanic. Web runtime evidence capture is the first of Plan G's five capture surfaces; F002 (iOS), F003 (Android), F004 (Backend), and F005 (common harness) are queued.

Public surface shipped:
- WebEvidenceCollector(plan_dir, driver=None, clock=None) with collect(journey, base_url, session_config) -> list[EvidenceRef]
- WebJourneyStep + WebSessionConfig + WebDriver + WebSession (Protocol) + WebDriverError
- Default _PlaywrightDriver returns a typed skip in v1; production session-adapter wiring is deferred to a follow-up plan once F2 has demand for live captures. The swap-seam path (operator-supplied driver) is the supported route in G1, which fully exercises the EvidenceRef round-trip + path discipline.

Boundary kept tight per operator directive:
- zero claude/shared/** changes
- no MCP tool exposure (library-only per Plan G locked answer #2)
- no F2 audit/scoring logic — capture only (D002)
- operator-supplied base URL/config (D004 — greppable assertion that no http(s):// host literal appears in web.py)
- artifacts under evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/web/<journey-id>/... (D003 — path discipline via goal_governance_evidence_path)
- fixtures under scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/runtime_evidence/_fixture_web/

Skip discipline (acceptance #4) verified across four paths:
- driver init failure -> typed skip EvidenceRef
- unexpected driver fault (non-WebDriverError) -> typed skip
- empty base_url -> typed skip
- empty journey -> typed skip
- per-step navigate failure -> partial artifacts + per-step skip-reason file
Collector contract: never raises to caller. All 18 tests confirm.

EvidenceRef typing (D007 verified at lock holds in practice):
- screenshot.png -> type=screenshot
- dom.html -> type=file
- console.log -> type=log
- network.jsonl -> type=log
- trace.zip / video.webm -> type=file
- skip-reason*.txt -> type=log
All map to existing v1.4.0 EvidenceRef.type enum. No agent-conventions schema change needed.

Verification:
- 18 new tests (test_runtime_evidence_web.py); 1070 passed, 6 skipped cumulative (= 1052 Plan G lock baseline + 18). Zero regressions.
- ruff check + format clean
- python3 scripts/sanitization_check.py: 0 findings (786 files scanned)
- F1 plan still validates green; no cross-plan drift

How to apply: F002 (iOS), F003 (Android), and F004 (Backend) follow the same pattern locked here — collector class with a swap seam, typed EvidenceRef artifacts, skip-reason discipline, no orchestration in v1 (per their respective Dxxx invariants). G5 (harness) composes all four behind a uniform interface.

title: Plan G amendment — add F006 (G0) Minimum operator configuration surface
body:
Locked at amendment turn 2026-05-06 (after G1/F001 closed at commit 62cdce6).

Plan G expands from 5 features to 6:
- F006 (prose: G0) ships the operator-facing config UX the G adapters consume.
- F006 lands FIRST among the still-pending features (G2/G3/G4/G5 depend on it).
- G1/F001 stays as-is — it shipped with per-call config and does not depend on F006. The new global/project defaults layer is purely additive (per-call > project > global > fallback per D004).
- F002, F003, F004 declare depends_on=['F006']. F005 declares depends_on=['F001','F002','F003','F004','F006'].

Six lock answers from the operator (2026-05-06):
1. Inside Plan G (not a separate plan) — same harness layer, single commit sequence.
2. Feature ID = F006 in features.json; prose label = G0.
3. Dependency edges as listed above.
4. Precedence: per-call > project config > global config > hardcoded fallback. For runtime_evidence: per-call > project config > none (no global tier per D015).
5. Doctor checks: F006 ships the registration framework only; each adapter (G2-G5) registers its own per-source check during implementation.
6. Roles migration: legacy default_implementer/default_auditor stay readable; canonical write target is roles.implementer/roles.auditor/roles.goal_auditor; config show reports resolved view.

Two operator additions folded into F006 acceptance:
- roles.goal_auditor consumed by F1/F003 sufficiency_auditor._resolve_goal_auditor_agent (additive read; F1's locked behavior preserved).
- dontpanic setup is preview-by-default; mutation requires --yes for non-interactive consistency with other DontPanic write-side commands.

Why amend mid-plan: G1 shipped with per-call config (correct), but G2-G5 will need defaults so operators don't pass simulator id / Firebase project / android package on every dispatch. Adding F006 inside Plan G keeps the config UX tied to the harness layer, single close-out memo, single sequence to track. Separate plan would add bookkeeping without reducing risk.

How to apply: F006 implementation begins next per turn-by-turn cadence. After F006 closes, G2 starts. The amended sequence is G0 (F006) → G2 (F002) → G3 (F003) → G4 (F004) → G5 (F005), with G1 already done.

title: Credentials are pointers, never values — clarification of D005
body:
Locked at amendment turn 2026-05-06 alongside F006 design.

DontPanic config (global + per-project + per-call) stores ONLY pointers to credentials, never credential values themselves. This clarifies D005 ('no new credential storage') by enumerating allowed pointer shapes:

- `adc` — assume gcloud Application Default Credentials; DontPanic reads no token data, just notes that ADC should be used at call time.
- path-only references — e.g. `"./secrets/sa.json"` or `~/.config/firebase-sa.json` — operator-supplied filesystem path; the JSON contents stay on disk and are read by the adapter at call time.
- `env:NAME` — operator-supplied env-var name; the value lives in the shell, not in DontPanic config.

Forbidden in DontPanic config / state / logs / output paths:
- Bearer tokens, API keys, OAuth refresh tokens, service-account JSON contents (the actual secret bytes).
- Anything that looks like `password=`, `bearer `, `api_key=` or similar credential-bearing literal.
- Any field name containing `_token`, `_key`, `_secret` (matches the existing F022/agent_manifest invariant).

Why: credential storage is its own decision class with its own threat model (rotation, blast radius, logging hygiene). DontPanic is operator-facing infrastructure plumbing, not auth infrastructure. Folding credential storage in here would stretch scope and create operational debt.

How to apply: F006 acceptance includes greppable assertions that adapter / CLI source contains no credential-bearing literals; `dontpanic setup` refuses secret-shaped values for any pointer field at write time. Future adapters that need persistent auth (e.g., OAuth refresh tokens for a SaaS provider) ship as their own plan with explicit credential-storage design — not a Plan G amendment.

title: Runtime evidence is project-scoped — global config never carries runtime target defaults
body:
Locked at amendment turn 2026-05-06 alongside F006 design.

Global config (`~/.dontpanic/config.json`) may define agent roles (`roles.implementer`, `roles.auditor`, `roles.goal_auditor`) and other cross-project preferences. Global config MUST NOT carry runtime target defaults — base URLs, simulator names, Android package IDs, Firebase / Supabase project IDs, backend provider settings, or any other field that names a specific deployment surface.

Those belong in:
- per-project config (`<repo>/.dontpanic/dontpanic.json`) for the project's stable runtime evidence target;
- per-call overrides at the adapter call site for one-off captures.

Precedence for runtime_evidence: per-call > project config > none (no global tier).

Why: runtime targets are project-specific by definition. A global default base_url like `http://localhost:3000` would be wrong for any project that doesn't run on that port; a global Firebase project id would couple every project to one backend. The cross-project coupling defeats Plan G's project-agnostic invariant (D004) at the config layer.

How to apply: F006 enforces D015 via two independent mechanisms:
1. Pydantic — global `Config` model has no `runtime_evidence` field at all; setting it raises a validation error at config load.
2. Greppable test assertion — F006 acceptance includes a source-grep that confirms `runtime_evidence` is not declared on the global config schema.

If a future need surfaces (e.g., a multi-project orchestrator wanting one default backend across many projects), the answer is a NEW config tier (a workspace tier between global and project), not relaxing D015. That would be its own plan with its own decision.

title: F006 (G0) shipped — minimum operator configuration surface
body:
F006 / G0 closed at this commit. Implementation boundary held to the four locked answers from the F006 lock turn:

1. RolesConfig (implementer / auditor / goal_auditor) and RuntimeEvidenceConfig (web / ios / android / backend sub-models) Pydantic models live in scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/config/.
2. Global config (~/.dontpanic/config.json) gained optional roles: RolesConfig field. D015 enforced two ways: GlobalConfig.model_config.extra='forbid' refuses runtime_evidence at the Pydantic layer; greppable test_f006_config_setup_surface.test_greppable_global_config_source_has_no_runtime_evidence confirms no runtime_evidence field declaration in source.
3. Project config (<repo>/.dontpanic/dontpanic.json) gained optional roles AND runtime_evidence fields. dontpanic project config set runtime_evidence.* writes through; dontpanic config set runtime_evidence.* refuses with a message pointing the operator at the per-project command (D015).
4. New CLI subcommands wired into cli.py main(): config (show / set), project config (init / set with --overwrite), setup (preview-by-default; --yes mutates; non-interactive without flags refuses). dontpanic doctor extension: registration framework only via config.doctor_registry.register_doctor_check(); F006 ships only the python_version baseline check. Adapter-specific checks land with G2-G5 (D013) — greppable test confirms F006 source contains no playwright/xcrun/simctl/adb/firebase_admin references.

D014 enforced: setup.is_credential_pointer() accepts only adc / env:NAME / path-only shapes; rejects AWS-shaped / GitHub PAT / Bearer / OpenAI / Slack / password=value patterns. dontpanic setup --backend-auth refuses secret-shaped values with operator message at plan-time (before any preview output to avoid accidental log leakage). Greppable test_config_package_source_clean confirms config/ source contains no credential literals (with carve-out for the rejection-pattern constant).

F003 amendment: sufficiency_auditor._resolve_goal_auditor_agent now resolves the auditor through config.resolvers.resolve_role(plan_dir, 'goal_auditor'), which prefers explicit roles.goal_auditor and falls through to resolved auditor / legacy default_auditor / hardcoded codex when unset. F1's locked behavior (cross-vendor invariant + DONTPANIC_GOAL_AUDITOR_ALLOW_SAME_VENDOR override) preserved end-to-end.

Verification:
- New test module: 68 tests passing (test_f006_config_setup_surface.py).
- Full orchestrate suite: 1138 passed, 6 skipped, 0 regressions.
- ruff check + format clean.
- sanitization_check.py clean (794 files scanned).

Worktree boundary: changes confined to scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/{config/,global_config.py,project_config.py,cli.py,sufficiency_auditor.py,tests/test_f006_config_setup_surface.py} and this plan dir's features.json + decisions.jsonl. Zero diffs to claude/shared/, F1 plan dir, runtime_evidence/ adapter package (G1's territory), or unrelated modules.

Why: enables G2-G5 to consume operator-supplied per-project defaults (Firebase project, simulator id, Android package, base URL) without forcing per-call kwargs at every adapter call site. G1/F001 stayed as-is — its per-call config remains valid; project defaults are purely additive (per-call > project > global > fallback per D004).

Next: G2 (F002) iOS adapter implementation.

title: F002 (G2) shipped — iOS runtime evidence capture
body:
F002 / G2 closed at this commit. Implementation boundary held to the operator's directive:

1. Capture-only (D002): screenshot + per-step simulator log slice + per-session crash report drain. No audit / scoring / pass-fail.
2. Config-driven via F006 layering: per-call kwargs (simulator/scheme/app_bundle_id) > runtime_evidence.ios from project config > none. Resolution delegated to config.resolvers.resolve_runtime_evidence (D015 — no global tier).
3. xcrun simctl as the default driver surface. _SimctlDriver lazy-checks shutil.which('xcrun') and refuses to open a session when xcrun is absent or simulator is unspecified, raising IosDriverError that the collector translates to a typed skip-reason EvidenceRef. Production simctl session adapter (boot, screenshot --type=png, simctl spawn log show, ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports enumeration) deferred to a follow-up plan; G2 v1 ships the swap-seam for stub/operator drivers, mirroring G1's Playwright-deferred posture.
4. Graceful skip: empty journey, driver init failure, activate_step / screenshot / log / crash drain failures all surface as typed EvidenceRef(type='log', note='skipped: ...'). Caller always gets a list back.
5. Evidence path: evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/ios/<journey-id>/{screenshot-<step>.png, log-<step>.log, crash-<name>, skip-reason*.txt} — composed via nested_orchestration.goal_governance_evidence_path (D003).
6. Typed EvidenceRef objects: type / uri (relative to plan_dir) / hash (sha256:hex) / captured_at / captured_by ('stub-ios-driver' or 'simctl-driver') / note. Compatible with G1/G0 surface; F2 (later) reads them as one heterogeneous list.
7. Fixture/mocked tests only: _StubSession + _StubDriver + static fixtures under tests/runtime_evidence/_fixture_ios/ (sample-screenshot.png, sample-simulator.log, sample-crash.crash). No live simulator dependency in pytest.
8. Doctor check ios_simctl registered idempotently via _register_ios_doctor_checks() at module import. Returns 'warn' (never 'fail') when xcrun is missing OR the simctl probe fails OR returns non-zero — so projects that don't target iOS aren't blocked. Greppable test asserts the warn-only contract across all failure modes.

Source-grep invariants enforced via tests:
- D003: greppable string `goal_governance_evidence_path(self._plan_dir, "post_impl", f"ios/{journey}")` present in source.
- D004: no project-name special cases (spin_dine_, glam_, creator_hub_).
- D005/D014: no credential-bearing literals (password=, Bearer prefix, api_key=) in module source.

Verification:
- 23 new tests in test_runtime_evidence_ios.py.
- Full orchestrate suite: 1161 passed, 6 skipped, 0 regressions.
- ruff check + format clean. sanitization_check.py clean (799 files scanned).

Worktree boundary: changes confined to scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/runtime_evidence/ios.py + tests/test_runtime_evidence_ios.py + tests/runtime_evidence/_fixture_ios/. Zero diffs to claude/shared/, F1 plan dir, F006 config package, runtime_evidence/web.py (G1's territory), Android/backend/harness layer (G3-G5 territory), or unrelated modules.

Next: G3 (F003) Android adapter — capture-only, two modes (passive-observe and post-hoc-ingest), no test orchestration in v1 per D009.

title: F003 (G3) shipped — Android runtime evidence capture
body:
F003 / G3 closed at this commit. Implementation boundary held to the operator's directive:

1. Capture-only (D002): no test orchestration. AndroidEvidenceCollector either watches a live device (passive_observe) or reads existing artifacts (post_hoc_ingest); never builds, installs, instruments, or invokes a test runner.
2. Two operator-selectable modes via AndroidSessionConfig.mode discriminator (Literal['passive_observe','post_hoc_ingest']):
   - passive_observe: per-step screenshot + logcat slice + per-session tombstones + ANR reports. Uses operator's existing emulator/device session via the driver swap seam.
   - post_hoc_ingest: scans operator-supplied artifact_dir for known Gradle/Espresso/Maestro/CI shapes (screenshots/, logcat/, logs/, tombstones/, anr/, test-results/). Wraps each as typed EvidenceRef. Unrecognized files silently skipped.
3. Config layering via F006 resolvers: per-call kwargs (package, adb_device_serial, artifact_dir) > runtime_evidence.android (project config) > none. D015 — no global tier; resolution delegated to config.resolvers.resolve_runtime_evidence.
4. Graceful skip: empty journey, driver init failure, activate_step / screenshot / logcat / tombstone / anr drain failures, missing/non-existent/empty artifact_dir, file-read errors during ingest — all surface as typed EvidenceRef(type='log', note='skipped: ...'). Caller always gets a list back.
5. Evidence path: evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/android/<journey-id>/{screenshot-<step>.png, logcat-<step>.log, tombstone-<name>, anr-<name>, ingest-<rel>, skip-reason*.txt} — composed via nested_orchestration.goal_governance_evidence_path (D003).
6. Typed EvidenceRef: type/uri/hash(sha256)/captured_at/captured_by ('stub-android-driver' or 'adb-driver' or specific operator driver). Compatible with G1/G2 surface; F2 reads them as one heterogeneous list.
7. Mocked/fixture tests only: _StubSession + _StubDriver + static fixtures under tests/runtime_evidence/_fixture_android/ (screenshots/, logcat/, tombstones/, anr/, test-results/, plus a random.dat that the ingest must skip). No live emulator dependency anywhere.
8. Doctor check android_adb registered idempotently via _register_android_doctor_checks(). Reports capability/readiness ONLY:
   - 'warn' when adb missing from PATH;
   - 'warn' when adb devices probe raises;
   - 'warn' when adb returns non-zero;
   - 'warn' when adb available but no devices attached;
   - 'pass' when adb available + at least one device attached.
   Never returns 'fail' — projects that don't target Android aren't blocked. Greppable test asserts the warn-only contract across all failure modes.

Source-grep invariants enforced:
- D003: greppable string `goal_governance_evidence_path(self._plan_dir, "post_impl", f"android/{journey}")` present in source.
- D004: no project-name special cases (spin_dine_, glam_, creator_hub_).
- D005/D014: no credential-bearing literals.
- D009: no test-orchestration tokens (gradle, gradlew, espressoRunner, am instrument, maestro test, maestro studio, androidx.test.runner).

Verification:
- 31 new tests in test_runtime_evidence_android.py (30 pass, 1 conditionally skipped on schema-permission edge).
- Full orchestrate suite: 1191 passed, 7 skipped, 0 regressions.
- ruff check + format clean. sanitization_check.py clean (808 files scanned).

Worktree boundary: changes confined to scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/runtime_evidence/android.py + tests/test_runtime_evidence_android.py + tests/runtime_evidence/_fixture_android/. Zero diffs to claude/shared/, F1 plan dir, F006 config package, runtime_evidence/{web,ios}.py (G1/G2 territory), backend/harness layer (G4/G5 territory), or unrelated modules.

Next: G4 (F004) backend adapter — provider-adapter pattern (Firebase ships first via F022 SA reuse; Supabase as provider slot + fixture tests only; Generic HTTP/log-file/JSONL fallback) per D010.

title: F004 (G4) shipped — backend runtime evidence capture (provider-adapter)
body:
F004 / G4 closed at this commit. Provider-adapter pattern per D010. Implementation boundary held to the operator's directive:

1. BackendEvidenceCollector + provider adapters: collector itself is provider-neutral; it walks the F006 config layers, picks the registered provider by name, dispatches probes, writes typed EvidenceRefs. Per-provider modules implement the live capture surface.
2. Three providers in v1:
